name: Hidden heel lifts / insoles

lead: Hidden heel lifts and height insoles are removable inserts that raise you roughly one to three centimetres inside normal shoes, so the added height does not show from outside. The gain is immediate and lasts while they are worn.

The insert raises the heel, lifting the whole body by its thickness. Some are full-length insoles and others are heel cups. Heel lifts have clinical trials for conditions such as mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy, but cosmetic use for height has not been the subject of published trials.

paras: People slip them into shoes with enough depth, often choosing thinner lifts for dress shoes and sneakers, and use them with outfits where a platform would stand out. Shoe fit is the main practical consideration, along with keeping them from showing at the heel.
Altering foot position changes loading and fit, and shoes may feel less stable or tight at the heel. Detection is a common concern, and long-term cosmetic use has not been studied in trials.

angle.text: Hidden heel lifts and height insoles add roughly one to three centimetres of height while worn, inside ordinary shoes and without the look of a platform. The gain is immediate and measurable; trials exist for medical heel lifts, not cosmetic use.

lead: Hidden heel lifts and height insoles are removable inserts placed inside ordinary shoes to raise the wearer by roughly one to three centimetres without the visible platform of high heels. Shoes with thickened insoles or built-up heels made to make the wearer look taller are called elevator shoes.[1]

Heel lifts are also used medically: a randomised trial compared heel lifts with calf eccentric exercise for mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy,[2] and older orthopaedic literature discusses leg length discrepancy after hip replacement.[3] Their cosmetic use for height is not the subject of published trials.
infobox: Not a regulated cosmetic height device

paras: Lifts are made of plastic, rubber or foam and sit under the heel or the full foot, so the height-adding component is hidden inside the shoe.[1] Some are full-length insoles with a graded wedge, others are small heel cups.

Heel lifts are used clinically for Achilles tendon problems and to compensate for leg length differences.[2][3] A randomised trial of heel lifts versus calf eccentric exercise for mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy examined these inserts as treatment, not as a cosmetic aid.[2]

Podiatry and sports-medicine literature discusses how altering foot position can change muscle activity and loading, as in a study of foot wedging and low back muscle activity during walking.[4] The effects of larger lifts worn long term for cosmetic purposes have not been studied in trials. Users in forums mention fit problems and instability in shoes as the main trade-offs.
Height insoles are a common low-cost tool in height discussion because they raise apparent stature immediately. Users on looksmax.org discuss being noticed wearing them and ways to avoid it.[5]
No studies found on cosmetic height insoles. Heel lifts have been studied clinically for Achilles tendinopathy,[2] which is a different use.

lore.intro: Hidden lifts are discussed as the quickest and most reversible way to appear taller, with focus on avoiding detection.
